objective: Add an opt-in initiative policy that creates a scoped Git commit after a work item successfully passes pi-swe completion gates, without pushing or including unrelated changes.

in: Workflow schema support for an opt-in per-initiative work-item auto-commit policy
Post-completion Git preflight, scoped staging, commit creation, and actionable failure reporting
Tool and command integration, documentation, and focused regression tests
out: Unconditional commits for initiatives without the policy
Committing unrelated user changes, runtime logs, or .gitignore
Changing evidence requirements or initiative finalization semantics

constraints: The policy must be explicit in workflow authority and default to disabled.
A commit may run only after evidence-gated work-item completion succeeds.
Use repository Git state and stage only paths attributable to the completed work item plus its workflow authority.
Never push automatically and never bypass existing command permissions or Git safety expectations.
A commit failure must leave the completed item durable and report clear recovery instructions without claiming a commit occurred.
Preserve unrelated staged and unstaged user changes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A validated initiative can opt into work-item auto-commit through a closed, documented policy field, while omitted or disabled policy values preserve current behavior.
Successful work-item completion under the enabled policy creates one concise commit containing only attributable task changes and the updated workflow authority, and never pushes.
Dirty-tree ambiguity, unrelated changes, Git failures, empty scoped changes, and disabled policy behavior are handled safely with actionable output and no false commit claim.
Focused pi-swe tests, typecheck, repository checks, and the full test suite pass, and user-facing pi-swe documentation describes policy semantics and limitations.

assessment.reason: This changes durable workflow schema and couples evidence-gated lifecycle mutation to Git side effects, requiring careful scope and failure semantics.
unknowns: The existing work model may need an explicit path allowlist to attribute changes safely.
Pi extension APIs may require the Git action to be surfaced as a model-performed follow-up rather than an internal subprocess.

practices.practice: Opt-in closed-schema policy with backward compatibility
practices.reason: Existing initiatives must retain current behavior and malformed policy values must fail validation.

practices.practice: Scoped Git safety and explicit failure semantics
practices.reason: Automation must preserve unrelated user state and never imply atomicity that Git and workflow persistence cannot provide.
Lifecycle, persistence, command output, and Git fixture behavior require regression coverage.

obligations.text: Test policy validation, persistence, and backward-compatible disabled behavior.
Test successful scoped commits and safe handling of unrelated changes, empty scope, and Git failures in isolated repositories.
Run typecheck, repository checks, focused pi-swe tests, and the full test suite after documentation is current.
Perform a source-bound model self-review of schema compatibility, permission behavior, path scoping, failure recovery, and documentation accuracy.

testing.approach: Add domain validation and isolated Git integration tests before implementing the completion hook, then run focused and repository-wide qualification.
testing.reason: The behavior combines schema compatibility, lifecycle state, and Git side effects, so negative fixtures are as important as the successful path.

evidence.summary: Model self-review (not independent or human approval): no blocking findings. The optional closed-schema policy preserves omitted/disabled behavior and participates in contract fingerprints; enabled mappings cover every executable leaf and reject unsafe, wildcard, Git metadata, .gitignore, and log paths. Completion remains evidence-gated and durable before commit preparation. Git execution is delegated to the ordinary bash permission boundary, uses a temporary index and literal scoped paths plus workflow.json, preserves unrelated staged/unstaged paths outside the declared scope, never pushes, and reports empty scope or hook/Git failures without claiming or reverting completion. Tests exercise schema negatives, default-disabled preparation, isolated-index success, unrelated staged preservation, no-push command generation, empty scope, hook failure, and service completion integration. README documents declared-directory attribution and non-atomic recovery semantics.

decisions.text: Work-item commits are opt-in per initiative and never push automatically.
Commit failures leave the already completed work item durable and must return recovery guidance.
decisions.basis: User-approved semantics and the lack of an atomic transaction spanning workflow persistence and Git.

risks.text: Automatic staging could capture unrelated user changes.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit attributable paths and test mixed dirty worktrees.

risks.text: Git commit hooks or failures can occur after workflow completion.
risks.mitigation: Keep completion durable, report the uncommitted state accurately, and provide retry guidance.

risks.text: Direct subprocess execution could bypass Pi command permission policy.
risks.mitigation: Inspect native Pi APIs and route through the ordinary approved command surface or a permission-preserving mechanism.
